blocks.text: Computer networks are classified by their size and coverage area. Different types are used for different purposes, and each connects devices in its own way. The most common types are the LAN, the WAN and the Internet (a public WAN). Understanding the types helps in choosing the right network.

blocks.title: Do you know?
blocks.text: Computer networks are classified on the basis of distance and coverage area.

blocks.caption: Types of computer network
rows: A small area: a home, school or office
High data-transfer speed; usually owned and managed by one organisation; uses Ethernet and Wi-Fi; cost-effective and easy to maintain
A large geographic area: different cities or countries
Uses leased lines, satellites or the Internet; slower than a LAN; expensive to install and manage
The largest WAN, joining millions of devices; uses standard protocols; supports email, websites and cloud storage for education, business and entertainment

blocks.title: Class activity
blocks.text: List services that use the Internet and discuss its importance.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: DSL (Digital Subscriber Line) gives Internet access through telephone lines and allows calling and browsing at the same time. An ISP (Internet Service Provider) is a company that provides Internet access to users.
